title: Get Beyond Learning Styles
coreMove: Choose representations and practice demands from the material, prior knowledge, and task, not from a learner’s preferred style label.
sourcePressure: The chapter rejects matching instruction to preferred learning styles while preserving real learner differences: prior knowledge, language fluency, structure building, and active processing matter.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The writer must avoid one-size-fits-all teaching; the chapter replaces style labels with evidence about content fit and learner preparation.

sourceAnchors.name: Robert Sternberg
sourceAnchors.detail: Psychologist whose examples include Brazilian orphans doing street-business math and horse-track handicappers building complex betting models while testing average on standard IQ measures.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Robert Sternberg’s street sellers and handicappers make the label less useful than the work a mind is being asked to do.

sourceAnchors.name: Bruce Hendry
sourceAnchors.detail: The chapter uses Hendry’s early lesson about scarce fireworks and later boxcar reasoning as an example of building richer mental models from prior knowledge.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Bruce Hendry did not need a visual label; he needed a supply-and-demand structure he could carry from fireworks to boxcars.

sourceAnchors.name: learning-styles empirical reviews
sourceAnchors.detail: The source notes state that matching instruction to a preferred style has not been confirmed by empirical research.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A preference can tell you what feels comfortable; it cannot by itself tell you what will be remembered or transferred.

hook: Do not open by saying learning is harder than it looks
Do not use a generic desk-and-notes image
Do not start with a broad claim about students today
counterintuition: Do not use the shell easier is not better
Do not flatten the chapter into struggle is good
Do not contrast comfort and growth in generic coaching language
tryThisNow: Do not write set a timer and reflect
Do not ask for a vague study audit
Do not use a reusable close-your-notes prompt without a chapter-specific action
examples: No repeated mug, marker, dosing cup, bike helmet, radiator, bus depot, classroom, or narrow-kitchen shells
No six examples that all start with a timestamp and a named protagonist
No generic student rereads notes scene unless the visible beat changes the method

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective reveal, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: Emily, a biology lecturer redesigning osmosis instruction
exampleSpecs.audience: teachers tempted to sort students into visual or verbal groups
exampleSpecs.stakes: students must predict membrane behavior on a novel lab question
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she chooses a diagram, a physical membrane demo, and a retrieval prompt because osmosis requires movement and pressure differences, not because students voted for visuals
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Two beakers sit on a lab bench with a sagging membrane between them.

exampleSpecs.domain: David, a safety trainer teaching lockout-tagout
exampleSpecs.audience: industrial trainers with mixed prior knowledge
exampleSpecs.stakes: a mislabeled energy source can injure someone
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he checks what trainees already know, then pairs a real disconnect box with a recall step instead of offering three style versions
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A red lock hangs from the disconnect switch.

exampleSpecs.domain: Chloé, a piano teacher explaining polyrhythm
exampleSpecs.audience: arts instructors deciding when sound, notation, and movement each help
exampleSpecs.stakes: the student can clap it but cannot transfer it to the keyboard
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she asks the student to tap, count, and notate the same rhythm because the material needs multiple representations tied to retrieval
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Show me where the three lands against the two," Chloé says.

exampleSpecs.domain: Mikkel, a data-science mentor teaching model overfitting
exampleSpecs.audience: technical mentors whose learners prefer videos but need diagnosis skill
exampleSpecs.stakes: the junior analyst must detect overfitting in a new dataset
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he has the learner predict model behavior on fresh data before showing the graph, making the task demand drive the representation
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Which curve lies when the training score looks perfect?

exampleSpecs.domain: Isabel, a literacy coach supporting multilingual readers
exampleSpecs.audience: educators balancing learner differences without style mythology
exampleSpecs.stakes: students need vocabulary, background knowledge, and retrieval practice before the text will open up
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show the shift from style grouping to a prep routine that builds background knowledge, key terms, and oral retrieval
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Isabel three reading groups to stop asking who was visual.

exampleSpecs.domain: Akira, a climbing instructor teaching route reading
exampleSpecs.audience: coaches whose students prefer watching demonstrations
exampleSpecs.stakes: the climber must choose holds under changed conditions
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he uses a route diagram only after the climber predicts the sequence from the wall, tying representation to discrimination
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 8:05 p.m., Akira points to the blank wall before the route card.

skillTargets: replace style matching with representation fit
include learner differences through prior knowledge and task demands
test whether a representation improves transfer rather than comfort

tryThisNowSpec: Pick one lesson you are planning and write: what the material demands, what the learner already knows, and what retrieval check will prove it.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
